outcomes.question: For corporate income tax, how does our company adjust donations to approved IPCs and other charities in its tax computation? Explain the enhanced deduction period and what the company must give the IPC.
outcomes.answer:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

#### IRAS — Corporate income tax

**Status:** Evidence verified

**Corporate income tax treatment of approved donations** (party in scope: Company)
- **IRAS rule explanation:** Donations are non-deductible expenses in arriving at adjusted profit. For donations made from 1 January 2016 through 31 December 2029, a company may claim a deduction of 2.5 times the amount donated to an approved Institution of a Public Character (IPC) or the Singapore Government to benefit the local community. The company must provide its UEN to the approved IPC. IRAS says approved donation amounts are pre-filled in Form C-S, Form C-S (Lite) or Form C based on information obtained from IPCs. In the tax computation, add back all donations, then deduct 2.5 times approved donations; the deduction is on a preceding-financial-year basis. The 2.5-times deduction applies to donations made from 1 January 2016 through 31 December 2029 under the captured current guidance. The donee must be an approved IPC or the Singapore Government, and a Government donation must benefit the local community. For an IPC donation, the company must provide its UEN to the IPC to receive the deduction. Approved donations are considered on a preceding-financial-year basis. Donations outside the approved-donation category remain non-deductible business expenses under this cited rule. This record does not cover individual income-tax donations, other incentive schemes, tax-exemption computation, or whether a named donee is currently approved. For case-specific application, consider: Donation date and financial year. Donee identity and current approved-IPC status, or whether a Singapore Government donation benefits the local community. Donation amount and the amount recorded by IRAS; whether the company provided its UEN to the IPC. This guidance does not calculate the company’s adjusted profit, chargeable income or tax deduction amount. Confirm that the donee and donation are eligible and reconcile the amount with the applicable YA before filing. [IRAS | Tax Treatment of Business Expenses (A-F)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/corporate-income-tax/income-deductions-for-companies/business-expenses/tax-treatment-of-business-expenses-(a-f))

**Source:** IRAS | Tax Treatment of Business Expenses (A-F) (live external)
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Corporate income tax treatment of approved donations): Donations
Donations are non-deductible expenses as they are not incurred in the production of income.
However, for donations made from 1 Jan 2016 to 31 Dec 2029*, you can claim a tax deduction of 2.5 times the amount donated to an approved Institution of a Public Character (IPC) or the Singapore Government to benefit the local community
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Corporate income tax treatment of approved donations): Your company is required to provide its Unique Entity Number (UEN) to the approved IPC in order to be given a tax deduction on the approved donations.
To enhance your filing experience, the approved donation amounts will be pre-filled in the Form C-S/ Form C-S (Lite)/ Form C
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Corporate income tax treatment of approved donations): Step 1: Add back all donations made (approved donations or otherwise) to arrive at the adjusted profit as donations are non-deductible expenses.
Step 2: Claim a tax deduction of 2.5 times the amount of approved donations. You can check the amount of approved donations made by the company via the View Donations digital service at mytax.iras.gov.sg. Tax deduction on approved donations is allowable on a preceding financial year basis
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports Corporate income tax treatment of approved donations): Tax deduction on approved donations is allowable on a preceding financial year basis.
- Official source: [IRAS | Tax Treatment of Business Expenses (A-F)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/corporate-income-tax/income-deductions-for-companies/business-expenses/tax-treatment-of-business-expenses-(a-f))

#### CPF Board — CPF contributions

**Status:** Evidence incomplete

**CPF contribution wage-record rectifications and refund or adjustment options** (party in scope: Employer)
- **CPF rule explanation:** Rectification depends on the error. Employers must rectify omitted or underpaid CPF contributions immediately, using the usual monthly contribution submission for arrears; delay can increase late-payment interest. If wages were declared incorrectly, inform CPF Board and ensure future submissions are accurate. For overpaid contributions, apply for a refund or adjustment. A refund returns excess money, while an adjustment changes the contribution record; CPF Board lists changing the contribution month or year, CPF Submission Number, or payment recipient as adjustment examples. Underpayment or omitted contributions are rectified immediately through the normal monthly submission process. Incorrect declared wages should be reported to CPF Board; future submissions must be accurate. For overpayment, choose refund when seeking excess money back or adjustment when correcting the contribution record. This procedure guide does not determine the correct wage classification, contribution rate, or amount owed in a particular payroll case. Overpaid contribution refunds remain subject to the separate refund process and its conditions. For case-specific application, consider: What was wrong: contribution amount, wages declared, contribution month/year, CSN or recipient. The affected employee, correct wage and contribution period, payment details, and whether money should be returned or only the record changed. No contribution amount, refund deadline, or case acceptance is calculated by this general rectification rule. Use the current application route for the employer type and error category. outcomes.question: For our Employment Act-covered staff, how long must we keep itemised payslips for current employees and employees who have left, and are electronic records allowed?
outcomes.answer:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

**Whole-question status:** Verified general guidance is available. Evidence verified for mapped issues; full request coverage unconfirmed.

**General statutory guidance:** Verified for all listed issues.
**Individual applicability:** General guidance does not by itself establish eligibility or compliance in an individual case.
**Material evidence gaps:** None identified within the listed guidance. Full request coverage still requires an independent assessment.

#### Ministry of Manpower — Employment requirements

**Status:** Evidence verified

**MOM itemised payslip content, delivery format and retention requirements** (party in scope: Employer)
- **MOM rule explanation:** Employers must issue itemised pay slips to employees covered by the Employment Act together with payment. If that is not possible, the pay slip must be given within three working days of payment. For termination or dismissal, it must be given together with outstanding salary. MOM allows a soft or hard copy, including handwritten. The pay slip must include the employer and employee names, payment date, basic salary, salary period, applicable allowances, other payments, deductions and total net salary; overtime hours, pay and period are included where applicable. If payments are made more than once a month, pay slips may be consolidated, but the consolidated slip must show all payments since the last slip. Employers must retain issued pay slips: the latest two years for current employees, and the last two years for ex-employees for one year after they leave. The requirements apply to employees covered by the Employment Act. Only applicable pay slip items need to be shown; overtime items 9 to 11 need not be included when overtime pay does not apply. The fallback is three working days after payment only when the employer cannot give the pay slip with payment. Consolidation is permitted for multiple monthly payments, but must include every payment since the previous slip. Items that do not apply need not be shown; MOM’s page gives overtime items as an example. This rule does not calculate final-salary deadlines or determine Employment Act coverage for a particular worker. For case-specific application, consider: Employment Act coverage. Salary period, payment date and pay components applicable to the employee. Whether pay slips are consolidated, whether overtime applies, current or former employee status, and the employee’s departure date if applicable. Three working days are not converted into calendar days. The captured page does not establish current coverage of a particular worker or calculate a case-specific final salary. [Itemised pay slips](https://www.mom.gov.sg/employment-practices/salary/itemised-payslips)

**Source:** Itemised pay slips (live external)

- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports MOM itemised payslip content, delivery format and retention requirements): Pay slips must include the items below, unless an item is not applicable. For example, if overtime pay does not apply to you, your pay slip need not include items 9 to 11.

#### ACRA — Corporate filing and governance

**Status:** Evidence verified

**ACRA local-company registered office location, access, records and notices** (party in scope: Company)
- **ACRA rule explanation:** For a local company, the registered office is the official Singapore address where ACRA and others can send communications and notices and where company records and registers are kept. It must be open to the public for at least three hours on each business day and open and accessible during normal business hours on each business day. It need not be the place where the company carries on its business activities. The page is guidance for local-company registration via Bizfile. The source states both a minimum of three public-access hours each business day and public access during normal business hours. The registered office may differ from the place where business is carried on. This source does not establish registered-office requirements for foreign companies, LLPs, VCCs or other entity types. For case-specific application, consider: Entity type and whether it is a local company. The proposed Singapore address, public-access hours on business days, and where company records and registers will be kept. This is ACRA guidance for local-company registration; it does not establish every ongoing filing duty or requirements for other entity classes. A specific address conclusion requires the entity type, address and access arrangements. [Step 4.6: Registering a local company via Bizfile | Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority](https://www.acra.gov.sg/register/business/registering-different-business-structures/local-company/registering-via-bizfile/)

outcomes.question: Under the current MAS VCFM toolkit, how do the Form7 deadlines differ between ceasing a regulated activity and failing to commence an activity within six months of licence grant? What customer-obligation certification accompanies cessation?
outcomes.answer:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

**Whole-question status:** Verified general guidance is available. Evidence verified for mapped issues; full request coverage unconfirmed.

#### Monetary Authority of Singapore — Financial regulation

**Status:** Evidence verified

**VCFM Form 7 cessation and noncommencement notification** (party in scope: Company)
- **MAS rule explanation:** A VCFM must submit Form 7, Notice of Cessation of Business, if it ceases to carry on any or all regulated activities. For cessation, the toolkit says to notify MAS within 14 days after the cessation and accompany Form 7 with an audit certification, in no prescribed format, that the VCFM has fully discharged all customer obligations. A VCFM that has not commenced any or all regulated activities by the end of six months from the CMS licence grant must submit Form 7 immediately after that six-month period ends. The cessation deadline applies to cessation of any or all regulated activities. The non-commencement rule applies when any or all regulated activities have not commenced by the end of six months from the licence grant. Form 7 cessation filing includes the stated audit certification of discharged customer obligations. This is a VCFM notification in the toolkit; it does not say that Form 7 is a prior-approval application. The toolkit does not establish the same process for an LFMC or another CMS licence category. For case-specific application, consider: Confirm the licence holder is a VCFM. Whether the event is cessation or non-commencement, the regulated activity affected, and the cessation date or CMS licence grant date. For cessation, whether the required customer-obligations audit certification is available. Do not calculate the non-commencement date without the CMS licence grant date or convert “immediately” into an invented day count. This bounded rule does not cover other VCFM notifications, winding-up duties or client-specific cessation consequences.
